resources.string: Head-unit map destination (experimental)
Read the head-unit map\'s destination

Listens for AMap navigation broadcasts on the head unit. The diagnostic report lists which fields they carry, without places or coordinates. Nothing goes to the iPhone until you tap the send button. Only the destination can be passed: the iPhone plans its own route.
Also read the coordinates from the map\'s log (needs ADB)

The head-unit map broadcasts only the destination\'s region, but it logs the planned route with its coordinates. DiPlay reads that line through its ADB shell every few seconds, so the iPhone can be sent the exact place instead of a district. Needs ADB over the network to be set up.
Show the navigation debug window

A small draggable window on the car\'s screen showing what the map is telling DiPlay, including the raw text of each read from the head unit. Drag the title bar to move the window, tap it to send it to the strip CarPlay is not using and tap again to bring it back, hold it and drag to resize. Needs "display over other apps". The raw text holds your real destinations, so a diagnostic report carries it only with “Include the head unit\'s raw log in reports” on, in a section named for it.
DiPlay cannot display over other apps, so the window will not appear. Allow it in Android settings, or over ADB.
DiPlay · navigation debug — drag to move, tap to send beside CarPlay
Waiting for the head-unit map. Start navigating to a place in the car.
(%1$d older lines dropped)
Record unrecognised map log lines

For troubleshooting a car whose destination DiPlay cannot read. It widens what it looks for in the map\'s log and records the lines it does not understand. Turn it off once the destination is read correctly. The raw text holds your real destinations, so a diagnostic report carries it only with “Include the head unit\'s raw log in reports” on, in a section named for it.
Include the head unit\'s raw log in reports

Adds the map\'s log lines exactly as the car wrote them, as read while “Show the navigation debug window” or “Record unrecognised map log lines” is on. They hold your real destinations and coordinates. Off by default: turn it on to send a report to the developer, and off again before posting one in public. With it off, the report says only whether such lines were recorded.
Follow the head unit\'s route automatically

Whenever the head-unit map plans a route to a new place, DiPlay hands it to the iPhone at once, with no tap on the button below. A route planned again to the same stops is not sent twice, so a re-plan for traffic does not interrupt the iPhone. CarPlay has to be connected.
Forget the destination when the head unit stops

When the head-unit map arrives or the driver cancels, DiPlay drops the stored destination, so it is not handed over again. CarPlay has no command a car can use to end the iPhone\'s guidance, so the iPhone keeps navigating; stop it on the phone or on the CarPlay screen.
The head-unit map has stopped navigating. The iPhone keeps its own guidance until you end it there.
End the iPhone\'s guidance too (experimental)
Replays taps you record once, to press the iPhone\'s own "End route". CarPlay has no command for this, so DiPlay has to inject touch.

DiPlay cannot read the CarPlay picture, so it taps the recorded points without knowing what is under them. If the iPhone\'s layout changes — an iOS update, another map app, a different CarPlay width — the taps land somewhere else with no warning, which may start a call or change a setting. Record the sequence again after any such change.

Only while parked
Replays the taps only with the gearbox in P, read over ADB. A gear that cannot be read counts as moving. Turning this off lets a blind tap sequence run while you drive.
Bring the map to the front first
Opens the map app before tapping, so the screen matches the one you recorded. Without it, a tap may land on whatever CarPlay happens to be showing.
Wait after bringing the map forward
The only wait before the first tap. Long enough for the map to appear on the CarPlay window; too short and the first tap lands on the screen that was there before.

Start navigation on the iPhone first, so the "End route" button is on screen. After you tap Start, this page closes and the map is brought to the front. Then end the route on the CarPlay window as you normally would, in %1$d taps. DiPlay records where you tap and how long you pause, and the route really does end. A drag or a long press is not recorded.

Include the via points (experimental)

Chains the head unit\'s via points into the link, with the destination as the last stop. Only Apple Maps takes more than one stop. If the iPhone opens the wrong place, turn this off and send the destination alone. The route itself cannot be passed: the iPhone plans its own way between the stops.
This link takes one destination only, so the via points are dropped. Choose Apple Maps to keep them.

AMap asks for the vehicle type (car, electric, motorcycle) the first time it navigates for another app. No link can answer that for it: its documented parameters carry a place, not a vehicle. Set the car once in AMap on the iPhone — 我的 → 车主服务 → 添加爱车 — and it stops asking. Apple Maps does not ask at all.
Press the map\'s own "start guidance" (experimental)

A link can only hand a place over; AMap then opens its route preview and waits for 开始导航 to be pressed. DiPlay replays a tap you record once, so the drive starts without touching the screen. Calibrate it on the preview itself.
Wait before tapping
Time for the iPhone to open the map and draw the route preview. Too short and the tap lands on the old screen; too long and the drive starts late. A cold start is slower than a warm one.
Taps to record
Calibrate the start tap

Send a destination so the map opens its route preview, then come back and start this. DiPlay will close this screen; press 开始导航 on the CarPlay window exactly as you normally would. %1$d tap(s) will be recorded.
Not calibrated yet, so nothing is tapped. Record the tap for 开始导航 first.
Test the start tap now

Sends the last destination again so the map reopens its route preview, then waits the delay above and taps. Recording the sequence starts the drive, so the preview is gone by then and a bare replay would aim at a button that is no longer on screen. With the navigation debug window on, DiPlay closes this page and shows CarPlay first, and reports each tap in that window instead of as a notice here.
Pause between taps
As recorded

A recorded pause is whatever your finger happened to do. A panel animation takes a fixed time, so a fixed pause is often steadier: too short and the next tap lands before the screen has changed, too long and the drive starts late.
